case_name: State of Himachal Pradesh v Mushtaq Ahmad
respondent:
Mushtaq Ahmad
Supreme Court of India

26 March 2007
S.L.P. (Cr.) 1102 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : HON'BLE JUSTICE DR. ARIJIT PASAYAT
1. Challenge in this special leave petition is to the order passed by a Division Bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court dismissing the application filed by the petitioner- State u/s. 378(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
2. Grievance of the petitioner is that the application was dismissed summarily without indicating any reason. It is stated by learned counsel for the petitioner that this Court has in many cases deprecated the practice of such dismissal.
3. The High Court has not given any reasons for refusing to grant leave to file appeal against acquittal, and seems to have been completely oblivious to the fact that by such refusal, a close scrutiny of the order of acquittal, by the appellate forum, has been lost once and for all. holding: The High Court order dismissing the application without giving reasons is not sustainable.
The requirement of indicating reasons in such cases has been judicially recognized as imperative.
Reasons are live links between the mind of the decision taker to the controversy in question and the decision or conclusion arrived at.
Right to reason is an indispensable part of a sound judicial system, reasons at least sufficient to indicate an application of mind to the matter before Court.
